nodes.title: Genetic Engineering & Recombinant DNA Technology
prelimsNote: rDNA uses restriction enzymes (molecular scissors) and ligases to insert genes into vectors (plasmids).
CRISPR-Cas9: Cas9 is a molecular scissors enzyme guided by RNA to edit genes (UPSC 2019).
RNA interference silences genes; used for pest-resistant crops and therapies (UPSC 2019).
rDNA technology can transfer genes across species barriers — UPSC 2013 tested its scope; GM crops, insulin and vaccines are key products.

nodes.title: GM Organisms — Agriculture, Ethics & Biosafety Regulation
prelimsNote: GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee) under the Environment Protection Act 1986 approves GM organisms (UPSC 2015).
Bt cotton (Cry1Ac, 2002) is the only GM food/fibre crop commercialised; Bollgard-II has Cry1Ac + Cry2Ab against bollworm (UPSC 2021).
Bt brinjal: approved by GEAC in 2009, moratorium in 2010 (UPSC 2011–13).
GM mustard DMH-11 uses barnase–barstar for hybrid seed (male sterility); GEAC approved environmental release in 2022 (UPSC 2018).
Trap: GM mustard has 'genes of soil bacterium' giving pest resistance — false; it is for hybridisation and herbicide tolerance.

nodes.title: Human Genome Project & Genomic Medicine
prelimsNote: Human Genome Project completed in 2003 (~3 billion base pairs, ~20,000 protein-coding genes).
Genome India Project (2020, DBT): sequencing 10,000 genomes completed in 2024.
Genome sequencing helps identify disease genes, develop crop varieties faster and study evolutionary links (UPSC 2017).
Microsatellite DNA (short tandem repeats) is used to study evolutionary relationships among species and in DNA fingerprinting (UPSC 2023).
Denisovans: extinct archaic humans identified from DNA (UPSC 2019).

nodes.title: Stem Cell Research & Cloning — Science & Ethics
prelimsNote: Totipotent (zygote) > pluripotent (embryonic, iPSCs) > multipotent (adult) stem cells; iPSCs reprogrammed from adult cells (Yamanaka).
Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer (SCNT): cloning technique (Dolly, 1996) (UPSC 2017).
Mitochondrial replacement (pronuclear transfer) creates 'three-parent babies'; mitochondrial DNA is inherited from the mother only (UPSC 2020, 2021).
Stem cells are used in regenerative medicine; ethical concerns centre on embryo use (UPSC 2012 tested stem-cell basics).

nodes.title: Bio-piracy & Traditional Knowledge Protection
prelimsNote: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL, 2001, CSIR + AYUSH) blocks wrongful patents (turmeric, neem, basmati cases).
Biological Diversity Act 2002 and Nagoya Protocol: access & benefit sharing; NBA approval for foreign access.
Patents Act 1970: biological processes for creating animals/plants not patentable (UPSC 2019).
TRIPS Art 27.3(b) allows exclusion of plants and animals but requires protection of plant varieties (India: PPV&FR Act 2001).

nodes.title: Bioinformatics & Precision Medicine
prelimsNote: DNA barcoding identifies species from short standard gene regions — distinguishes look-alike species and detects adulteration in food (UPSC 2022).
Aerial metagenomics collects DNA samples from air in a habitat in one go (UPSC 2023).
Transcriptome = full set of RNA transcripts in a cell (UPSC 2016).
Precision medicine tailors treatment to an individual's genetic profile.

nodes.title: Intellectual Property Rights — Patents, Copyright & TRIPS
prelimsNote: Patents Act 1970 (amended 2005 for TRIPS); Sec 3(d) bars evergreening (Novartis case, 2013).
Patent term 20 years; compulsory licensing (Natco–Bayer, 2012).
National IPR Policy 2016 — DPIIT is nodal (UPSC 2017).
GI Act 1999 enacted to comply with TRIPS (UPSC 2018); copyright: 60 years after the author's death for literary works.

nodes.title: Biotechnology in Medicine — Vaccines, Biosimilars & Gene Therapy
prelimsNote: Vaccine platforms (UPSC 2021, 2022): Covishield = viral vector (chimpanzee adenovirus), Sputnik V = viral vector, Covaxin = inactivated virus; Covishield is NOT mRNA.
Adenoviruses have double-stranded DNA genomes (UPSC 2021).
Biosimilars are near-copies of approved biologic drugs; generics copy small-molecule drugs.
Gene therapy can treat genetic disorders by correcting/replacing genes; CAR-T therapy (India's NexCAR19, 2023) re-engineers T cells against cancer.
Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (UPSC 2020): India's indigenous PCV; protects against pneumonia, meningitis, sepsis.

nodes.title: Nanotechnology — Principles, Applications & India's Nano Mission
prelimsNote: Nanoscale = 1–100 nm; high surface-area-to-volume ratio and quantum confinement change properties.
Graphene: single layer of carbon atoms, strongest and highly conductive (UPSC 2012); carbon nanotubes used for drug carriers, artificial blood capillaries, biosensors (UPSC 2020).
Nano Mission (2007, DST).
Nanoparticles occur naturally too (volcanic ash, sea spray) — UPSC 2022 statement that they exist only as man-made was false.

nodes.title: Nanotechnology in Medicine, Agriculture & Environment
prelimsNote: Nano-urea and nano-DAP (IFFCO) reduce fertiliser use.
Nanoparticles of metal oxides (TiO₂, ZnO) are used in cosmetics and sunscreens; some nanoparticles entering the environment are unsafe (UPSC 2022).
Nanotech in health (UPSC 2015): targeted drug delivery, gene therapy.
Carbon fibres used in automobile and aircraft components; they CAN be recycled (UPSC 2023).

nodes.title: Cyber Warfare & Electronic Intelligence
prelimsNote: Ransomware (WannaCry, Petya 2017 — UPSC 2018) encrypts data for ransom; spyware like Pegasus exploits zero-day vulnerabilities.
CERT-In (IT Act Sec 70B) is the national nodal agency; 2022 directions require reporting cyber incidents within 6 hours (UPSC 2017 asked about mandatory reporting).
NCIIPC (Sec 70A) protects Critical Information Infrastructure; Defence Cyber Agency set up in 2019.
Cyber insurance can cover data-restoration costs, extortion payments and third-party liability (UPSC 2020).

nodes.title: Artificial Intelligence — Applications, Ethics & Governance
prelimsNote: AI capabilities tested (UPSC 2020): reducing electricity consumption, creating meaningful short stories, disease diagnosis, text-to-speech — all possible.
Machine learning learns patterns from data; generative AI (LLMs) creates text/images; deepfakes are synthetic media.
IndiaAI Mission (2024): compute capacity (GPUs), datasets, indigenous foundation models.
Trap: AI is not 'programmed rules only' — it can learn without explicit programming.

nodes.title: Cybersecurity — Threats, Laws & National Cyber Policy
prelimsNote: IT Act 2000 (amended 2008) — Sec 66A struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015).
Digital signatures (UPSC 2019): authenticate the signer, identify the document and are legally valid under the IT Act; PKI provides the key infrastructure (UPSC 2020).
Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 created the Data Protection Board.
National Cyber Security Policy 2013 (a new strategy has been under preparation).

nodes.title: Internet Governance — Net Neutrality, Data Sovereignty
prelimsNote: Net neutrality: TRAI's Prohibition of Discriminatory Tariffs (2016) blocked zero-rating like 'Free Basics'; DoT accepted net-neutrality rules in 2018.
Data localisation: RBI (2018) requires payment data stored only in India (UPSC 2019).
ICANN manages the domain-name system; the Internet Governance Forum is UN-convened.
DPDP Act 2023 allows cross-border data transfer except to countries the government blacklists.

nodes.title: Big Data & Cloud Computing — Governance Applications
prelimsNote: Cloud models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS — SaaS buyers can customise the user interface and data fields; Outlook, Hotmail, Yahoo! Mail are SaaS (UPSC 2022).
MeghRaj: GoI's cloud initiative.
Big data: volume, velocity, variety (and veracity); used in governance analytics.
Edge computing processes data near the source to cut latency.

nodes.title: Blockchain Technology — Uses, Cryptocurrency & Regulation
prelimsNote: Blockchain (UPSC 2020): a public ledger everyone can inspect but no single user controls; its data is NOT only about cryptocurrency; applications can be built on it without anyone's permission.
Bitcoin (UPSC 2016): peer-to-peer, no central authority; not legal tender in India.
NFTs (UPSC 2022) are unique tokens on a blockchain; they are not interchangeable at equivalency.
Crypto income taxed at 30% with 1% TDS (Budget 2022); CBDC (e₹) issued by RBI is legal tender.

nodes.title: Internet of Things (IoT) & Cyber-Physical Systems
prelimsNote: IoT: network of devices that sense, communicate and act without human intervention (UPSC 2018).
Wearables (UPSC 2019) can track location, heart rate and other vitals.
Accelerometer detects acceleration/tilt — airbag deployment, laptop free-fall protection, screen rotation (UPSC 2023).
IoT security risk: large attack surface (botnets such as Mirai).

nodes.title: Social Media — Regulation, Misinformation & Internal Security
prelimsNote: IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules 2021: grievance officers, traceability of first originator for significant intermediaries.
Sec 69A of the IT Act allows blocking of online content (upheld in Shreya Singhal 2015).
Sec 79: safe-harbour for intermediaries that follow due diligence.
Deepfakes and AI-labelling advisories issued by MeitY (2023–24).

nodes.title: E-Governance — Digital India, NeGP & Service Delivery
prelimsNote: NeGP (2006) → Digital India (2015): digital infrastructure, governance & services on demand, digital empowerment.
DigiLocker: digital locker under Digital India; documents accessible anywhere (UPSC 2016).
Aarogya Setu, CoWIN, DigiLocker and DIKSHA are built on open-source platforms (UPSC 2022).
Aadhaar (UIDAI, statutory under the Aadhaar Act 2016); BHIM-UPI; Common Service Centres for rural delivery.

nodes.title: 5G Technology — Applications, Security Concerns & Rollout
prelimsNote: 5G launched in India in October 2022; uses sub-6 GHz and mmWave bands; enables network slicing and low latency.
LTE is data-only; VoLTE carries voice over LTE (UPSC 2019).
Short-range technologies (UPSC 2022): CCTV, RFID, Wireless LAN.
Li-Fi/VLC use visible light (UPSC 2016, 2020); Project Loon used balloons for internet (UPSC 2016).
Telecommunications Act 2023 replaced the Indian Telegraph Act 1885.

nodes.title: Semiconductor Industry — India's Chip Policy & Fab Ecosystem
prelimsNote: India Semiconductor Mission (2021, ₹76,000 crore) under Digital India Corporation.
First fab: Tata–PSMC at Dholera (approved 2024); OSAT units by Micron (Sanand) and others.
Semiconductors: silicon, germanium; doping creates n-type and p-type; LEDs are semiconductor devices.
Rare earths and critical minerals are strategic inputs (National Critical Mineral Mission 2025).

nodes.title: Quantum Computing — Principles & National Mission
prelimsNote: Qubits exploit superposition and entanglement — 'qubit' is the term from quantum computing (UPSC 2022).
National Quantum Mission (2023, ₹6,003 crore): 50–1,000 qubit computers by 2031, quantum communication and sensing.
Quantum key distribution offers theoretically unbreakable encryption.
Trap: quantum computers do not replace classical ones for all tasks.

nodes.title: Robotics & Automation — Industry 4.0 & Employment Impact
prelimsNote: Industry 4.0: cyber-physical systems, IoT, AI, 3D printing, robotics.
3D printing builds objects layer by layer from digital models (UPSC 2018).
Augmented reality overlays digital info on the real world; virtual reality creates a fully immersive environment (UPSC 2019).
Automation raises productivity but displaces routine jobs.

nodes.title: ISRO — History, Missions & Launch Vehicles
prelimsNote: ISRO founded 1969 (INCOSPAR 1962 under DAE); Department of Space 1972; first satellite Aryabhata (1975, Soviet launch); first Indian launch vehicle SLV-3 (1980, Rohini).
PSLV: 4 stages alternating solid–liquid–solid–liquid; workhorse for polar/sun-synchronous orbits (also launched Chandrayaan-1 and MOM).
GSLV uses an indigenous cryogenic upper stage (liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen) for GTO; LVM3 (GSLV Mk III) launched Chandrayaan-2/3 and is human-rated for Gaganyaan.

Trap (UPSC 2018): PSLV satellites (Earth observation) do not appear fixed in the sky; GSLV Mk III (LVM3) is a three-stage vehicle — solid strap-ons, liquid core, cryogenic upper stage — not four-stage.
SSLV (2022–23): small satellites (≤500 kg to LEO) with three solid stages + a liquid trim module (VTM).

nodes.title: Satellite Technology — INSAT, Remote Sensing & Applications
prelimsNote: Geostationary orbit ≈ 35,786 km above the Equator, period = 24 h, appears stationary — used for communication and weather (INSAT/GSAT); polar/sun-synchronous orbits (~500–800 km) for remote sensing (IRS, Cartosat, Resourcesat).
Remote sensing applications (UPSC 2019): crop acreage and yield estimates, groundwater prospecting, forest cover, disaster monitoring.
GPS/satellite applications: precision agriculture, disaster response, fleet tracking (UPSC 2018).
Active sensors (SAR/radar) work through clouds and at night; passive optical sensors need sunlight.
NISAR (NASA–ISRO SAR, L- and S-band) launched in 2025 (as of 2025) for Earth-surface change monitoring.

nodes.title: Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan & Gaganyaan — India's Space Missions
prelimsNote: Chandrayaan-1 (2008, PSLV) detected water/hydroxyl on the Moon with NASA's M3 payload; Chandrayaan-2 (2019) orbiter still working, lander Vikram crash-landed.
Chandrayaan-3 (2023, LVM3): first soft landing near the lunar south pole (Shiv Shakti point, 23 August = National Space Day).
Mangalyaan/MOM (2013, PSLV): India first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit and first in the world on its maiden attempt; it was NOT launched by GSLV (UPSC 2016).
Aditya-L1 (2023): solar observatory at the Sun–Earth Lagrange point L1 (~1.5 million km).
Gaganyaan: human spaceflight to ~400 km LEO on human-rated LVM3; crew module, uncrewed G1 test flights precede crewed flight (as of 2025).

nodes.title: Commercial Space — NewSpace India & Global Competition
prelimsNote: NewSpace India Ltd (NSIL, 2019): commercial arm of ISRO for launches, satellite services and technology transfer; Antrix (1992) is the older commercial arm.
IN-SPACe (2020): single-window regulator/promoter authorising private space activities.
Indian Space Policy 2023 opened the full value chain to private players; FDI rules liberalised in 2024 (up to 100% in satellite components via automatic route).
Private milestones: Vikram-S (Skyroot, 2022) first private sub-orbital launch; Agnikul's semi-cryogenic 3D-printed engine flight (2024).

nodes.title: GPS & Navigation Systems — NavIC & Geostrategic Importance
prelimsNote: NavIC (IRNSS): regional system of 7 satellites (3 GEO + 4 GSO) covering India and ~1,500 km around it (UPSC 2018).
Global systems: GPS (USA), GLONASS (Russia), Galileo (EU), BeiDou (China); Japan's QZSS is regional — UPSC 2023: Japan has its own satellite navigation system.
GAGAN (ISRO + AAI): satellite-based augmentation system improving GPS accuracy for aviation.
Trap: NavIC is regional, not global; it uses L5 and S bands.

nodes.title: Space Debris & International Space Law
prelimsNote: Kessler Syndrome: cascading collisions making orbits unusable.
Project NETRA (ISRO): space situational awareness network to track debris.
Mission Shakti (2019): India's anti-satellite (ASAT) test in LEO (~300 km) — chosen to limit long-lived debris.
Space law: Outer Space Treaty 1967 (no national appropriation, no WMD in orbit), Liability Convention 1972, Registration Convention 1975; Moon Agreement 1979 (few signatories).

nodes.title: Nuclear Energy — Reactor Types, India's Nuclear Programme
prelimsNote: Three-stage programme (Homi Bhabha): Stage 1 PHWRs on natural uranium, Stage 2 Fast Breeder Reactors on plutonium (breed fissile material), Stage 3 thorium-based reactors (U-233).
Heavy water (D₂O) is the moderator in PHWRs — slows neutrons (UPSC 2011).
India has large thorium reserves (monazite sands) but limited uranium (UPSC 2012).
Fission splits heavy nuclei (U-235, Pu-239); fusion joins light nuclei (deuterium–tritium) — ITER in France aims to demonstrate fusion; India is a member (UPSC 2016).
Small Modular Reactors (≤300 MWe) and Bharat Small Reactors announced with private participation in Budget 2025 (as of 2025).

nodes.title: Nuclear Safety — Accidents, Radiation & Public Concerns
prelimsNote: Major accidents: Three Mile Island (USA, 1979), Chernobyl (USSR, 1986), Fukushima (Japan, 2011 — tsunami-triggered).
Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB, 1983) regulates safety in India — created by executive order under the Atomic Energy Act 1962, not a statutory independent regulator.
Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010: operator liability, with right of recourse against suppliers (Sec 17) — a sticking point for foreign suppliers.
Radiation units: becquerel (activity), gray (absorbed dose), sievert (biological effect).

nodes.title: India-USA Nuclear Deal & NSG Waiver
prelimsNote: Joint statement 2005; 123 Agreement 2008 under the US Atomic Energy Act; NSG granted India a 'clean waiver' in Sept 2008.
India separated civil and military facilities; civil reactors placed under IAEA safeguards — some reactors use imported fuel, which must be safeguarded (UPSC 2020).
India signed the IAEA Additional Protocol (ratified 2014) — civil facilities under broader IAEA inspection (UPSC 2018).
NSG membership gives access to latest nuclear technology but does NOT make a country an NPT member (UPSC 2018); India is not yet an NSG member.

nodes.title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation — NPT, CTBT & India's Position
prelimsNote: NPT (1968, in force 1970): recognises 5 nuclear-weapon states (tested before 1 Jan 1967); India, Pakistan, Israel never signed; North Korea withdrew.
CTBT (1996) not in force — requires all 44 Annex-2 states to ratify; India has not signed.
Export-control regimes India has joined: MTCR (2016), Wassenaar Arrangement (2017), Australia Group (2018); not NSG (UPSC 2022).
New START (US–Russia, 2010) caps deployed strategic warheads (UPSC 2011); Russia suspended participation in 2023.
Nuclear Security Summits (2010–2016) were US-led, not under UN aegis; International Panel on Fissile Materials is independent, not an IAEA organ (UPSC 2017).

nodes.title: Solar Energy — Technology, Solar Mission & Grid Parity
prelimsNote: Solar PV converts light to electricity directly; solar thermal uses heat (UPSC 2014).
National Solar Mission (2010) target raised to 100 GW by 2022; India's 2030 target 500 GW non-fossil capacity.
Net metering lets rooftop solar households sell excess power to the grid (UPSC 2016); PM Surya Ghar (2024) rooftop scheme.
Materials: crystalline silicon dominates; perovskite and thin-film (CdTe, CIGS) are emerging.
International Solar Alliance launched at COP21 Paris (2015); HQ Gurugram.

nodes.title: Wind Energy — Offshore & Onshore Development
prelimsNote: India has ~45+ GW installed wind capacity, 4th largest globally (as of 2024).
Top wind states: Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra.
National Offshore Wind Energy Policy 2015; targets off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu coasts.
Wind–solar hybrid policy 2018 improves grid utilisation.

nodes.title: Nuclear Energy — Thorium Programme & Fast Breeder Reactors
prelimsNote: Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (500 MWe, Kalpakkam, BHAVINI) began core loading in 2024 — gateway to Stage 2.
Fast breeders produce more fissile material than they consume; use liquid sodium coolant.
Stage 3 uses thorium–U-233 cycle; Advanced Heavy Water Reactor (AHWR) design by BARC.
Thorium is fertile, not fissile — needs conversion to U-233 (UPSC 2012).

nodes.title: Hydrogen Energy — Green Hydrogen Policy
prelimsNote: Grey (from natural gas, emits CO₂), blue (with carbon capture), green (electrolysis using renewable power).
National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023): 5 MMT annual production by 2030; SIGHT incentive programme.
Green hydrogen can be used directly in internal combustion, blended with natural gas for heat/power, and in fuel cells for vehicles (UPSC 2023).
Expected to decarbonise fertiliser plants, oil refineries and steel plants (UPSC 2023).
Fuel cells produce electricity with water and heat as by-products (UPSC 2015); H-CNG blends hydrogen with CNG (UPSC 2019).

nodes.title: Biofuel — Ethanol Blending & Biogas Policy
prelimsNote: Generations: 1G (food crops), 2G (lignocellulosic residues), 3G (algae), 4G (engineered organisms with carbon capture).
National Policy on Biofuels 2018 (amended 2022): E20 target advanced to 2025-26 — achieved in 2025 (as of 2025); allows damaged grains, sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses (UPSC 2020).
SATAT (2018) promotes compressed biogas; GOBARdhan for cattle-dung biogas.
Algae biofuel constraints: large land/water needs, contamination, cost (UPSC 2017).

nodes.title: Energy Storage — Battery Technology & Grid Management
prelimsNote: Lithium-ion dominates; sodium-ion (cheaper, abundant sodium) and solid-state (safer, higher density) are emerging.
PLI for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) battery storage (2021).
Cobalt for EV batteries: ~70–75% of world supply from DR Congo (UPSC 2023).
Pumped-storage hydro and battery energy storage systems balance renewable variability; VGF for BESS (2023).

nodes.title: Nuclear Doctrine & Strategic Deterrence
prelimsNote: India's doctrine (2003): credible minimum deterrence, No First Use, massive retaliation, non-use against non-nuclear weapon states.
Nuclear Command Authority: Political Council (chaired by PM) authorises use; Executive Council (NSA) advises.
Nuclear triad completed with INS Arihant's first deterrence patrol (2018) — SSBN with K-series SLBMs.
Tests: Pokhran-I (1974, 'Smiling Buddha'), Pokhran-II (1998, Operation Shakti).

nodes.title: India's Missile Programme — Agni, Prithvi, BrahMos
prelimsNote: IGMDP (1983, APJ Abdul Kalam): Prithvi (SRBM), Agni (IRBM/ICBM), Trishul, Akash (SAM), Nag (anti-tank); concluded 2008.
Agni-V: ~5,000+ km ICBM-class, solid-fuelled, canisterised; MIRV test 'Mission Divyastra' (2024).
BrahMos (India–Russia JV): supersonic cruise missile (~Mach 2.8), not an ICBM; trap in UPSC 2023 swapped Agni-V and BrahMos descriptions.
Ballistic missiles are rocket-powered and follow a ballistic arc; cruise missiles are jet-powered and fly within the atmosphere — UPSC 2023 statement reversing this was false.
Agni-IV (UPSC 2014): ~4,000 km, solid-fuelled surface-to-surface missile.

nodes.title: DRDO — Role, Achievements & Indigenisation
prelimsNote: Set up in 1958 under the Ministry of Defence by merging defence science establishments.
Key products: Tejas LCA, Arjun MBT, Akash, Astra BVR AAM, Pinaka MBRL, ATAGS, Netra AEW&C.
Ballistic Missile Defence: Prithvi Air Defence (exo-atmospheric) and Advanced Air Defence (endo-atmospheric) interceptors.
Hypersonic: HSTDV scramjet demonstration (2020); long-range hypersonic missile test (Nov 2024).

nodes.title: Make in India in Defence — FDI, DPP & Offset Policy
prelimsNote: Defence FDI: up to 74% via automatic route, beyond 74% through government approval (2020).
Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020 replaced DPP; categories prioritise 'Buy (Indian-IDDM)'.
Positive Indigenisation Lists bar import of notified items after set timelines.
Defence corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu; iDEX (2018) funds defence start-ups.

nodes.title: Stealth Technology, Drones (UAVs) & Modern Warfare
prelimsNote: Stealth reduces radar cross-section through shaping and radar-absorbent materials.
Drone uses (UPSC 2020): agricultural spraying, mapping, crater inspection of volcanoes, breath sampling of whales.
Drone Rules 2021 and PLI for drones; Digital Sky platform for permissions.
Anti-drone systems (DRDO D4) use detection, jamming and laser 'hard kill'.
THAAD is a US terminal-phase missile defence system (UPSC 2018).

nodes.title: Chemical & Biological Weapons — Conventions & Threats
prelimsNote: Chemical Weapons Convention (1993, in force 1997) — implemented by the OPCW (The Hague), an independent body, not an EU/NATO/WHO organ (UPSC 2016).
OPCW monitors the chemical industry and assists states against chemical-weapons threats (UPSC 2016).
Biological Weapons Convention (1972) has no verification body like the OPCW.
Australia Group harmonises export controls on chemical/biological dual-use items; India joined in 2018.

newNodesToCreate.title: Everyday Science — Units, Instruments, States of Matter & Heat Transfer
prelimsNote: Water expands on freezing (anomalous expansion below 4 °C) — ice floats and pipes burst in winter (UPSC 2011).
Pressure cooker cooks faster because higher pressure raises water's boiling point (UPSC 2021).
Instruments: SONAR (sound under water), RADAR (radio waves), seismograph (earthquakes), barometer (air pressure), hygrometer (humidity).
Heat transfer: conduction (solids), convection (fluids), radiation (no medium needed).
Light-year is a unit of distance, not time (UPSC 2021); the outermost (non-luminous) zone of a flame is hottest (UPSC 2020).

newNodesToCreate.title: Optics & Electromagnetic Spectrum — Refraction, Dispersion, Scattering & Rainbow
prelimsNote: Rainbow involves refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection (UPSC 2013); refraction explains twinkling of stars, apparent bending of a stick in water.
Rayleigh scattering (∝ 1/λ⁴) makes the sky blue and the Sun red at sunrise/sunset.
EM spectrum by decreasing frequency: gamma > X-ray > UV > visible > infrared > microwave > radio.
Infrared is absorbed mainly by water vapour and CO₂ in the lower atmosphere — not part of the visible spectrum (UPSC 2023).
Displays: LED and OLED (organic, flexible, no backlight — UPSC 2017); LEDs are more efficient than CFLs and contain no mercury (UPSC 2011, 2021).

newNodesToCreate.title: Mechanics, Gravitation, Sound & Fundamental Forces
prelimsNote: Four fundamental forces: gravitational, electromagnetic, strong and weak nuclear (UPSC 2013).
Ball bearings reduce friction (rolling vs sliding) (UPSC 2013); gravity provides the centripetal force for satellites (UPSC 2011).
Escape velocity from Earth ≈ 11.2 km/s; geostationary period = 24 h.
Doppler effect: change in observed frequency with relative motion — red shift of galaxies indicates an expanding universe (UPSC 2012).
Higgs boson ('God particle') gives mass to particles — confirmed at CERN's LHC in 2012 (UPSC 2013).

newNodesToCreate.title: Electricity, Magnetism, Semiconductors & Superconductivity
prelimsNote: Metals conduct due to free electrons; non-metals lack free electrons (bad conductors).
Transformers work only on AC (mutual induction); superconductors have zero resistance below a critical temperature.
Semiconductors (Si, Ge): doping gives n-type and p-type; LEDs, solar cells and transistors are semiconductor devices.
Sodium lamps emit near-monochromatic yellow light; LEDs give a wider spectrum and longer life — UPSC 2021 compared the two.
Earth's magnetic field has reversed many times; the magnetosphere deflects the solar wind (UPSC 2012, 2018).

newNodesToCreate.title: Everyday Chemistry — Acids/Bases, Polymers, Plastics & Common Chemicals
prelimsNote: pH < 7 acidic, > 7 basic; acid rain is caused by SO₂ and NOx (UPSC 2022); some microbes grow below pH 3 (UPSC 2023).
Water is a universal solvent because of its polarity (UPSC 2021).
PET: fibres blend with wool/cotton and bottles are recyclable; incineration releases greenhouse gases (UPSC 2022).
Bisphenol A (BPA) in polycarbonate plastics is an endocrine disruptor (UPSC 2021); triclosan is an antimicrobial in toiletries (UPSC 2021).
Trans fats from partial hydrogenation raise LDL cholesterol (UPSC 2011); aspartame is an artificial sweetener (UPSC 2011).

newNodesToCreate.title: Elements, Radioactivity & Isotopes — Rare Earths, Heavy Metals & Critical Minerals
prelimsNote: Isotopes: carbon-14 (dating), iodine-131 (thyroid), cobalt-60 (cancer therapy), uranium-235 (fission).
Monazite contains thorium and rare earths; government bodies only can process/export it (UPSC 2022).
Ilmenite and rutile are titanium ores in coastal sands (UPSC 2023).
Heavy-metal pollution: mercury from gold mining and coal plants (UPSC 2023); lead from batteries and paints (UPSC 2012).
Critical minerals for batteries: lithium, cobalt, nickel, graphite; Lithium found in J&K (Reasi) in 2023.

newNodesToCreate.title: Cell Biology, Genetics Basics & Plant Physiology
prelimsNote: Plant cells have cell walls, large vacuoles and chloroplasts; animal cells lack cell walls (UPSC 2020).
Mitochondria have their own DNA, inherited only from the mother (UPSC 2021).
Girdling a tree cuts phloem — roots starve and the tree dies (UPSC 2011).
Photosynthesis: CO₂ + water + light → glucose + oxygen in chloroplasts; transpiration is water loss through stomata.
Plant hormones: auxins (growth), gibberellins (stem elongation), cytokinins (cell division), ethylene (ripening), ABA (stress).

newNodesToCreate.title: Human Physiology, Nutrition & Microorganisms
prelimsNote: Vitamin deficiencies: A — night blindness, B1 — beriberi, C — scurvy, D — rickets, K — poor clotting (UPSC 2014).
Blood groups follow ABO alleles; a child's group depends on parents' genotypes (UPSC 2011).
B cells make antibodies, T cells kill infected cells — both protect against pathogens (UPSC 2022).
Probiotics contain live bacteria and yeast; they occur naturally in the gut and help digest milk sugars (UPSC 2022).
Viruses lack cell machinery and are not killed by antibiotics; lichens are fungus–alga symbioses (UPSC 2013, 2014).

newNodesToCreate.title: Infectious Diseases, Antimicrobial Resistance & Disease Control
prelimsNote: Viral: COVID-19 (enters via ACE2 receptors — UPSC 2021), dengue, Zika (Aedes mosquito; also sexual transmission — UPSC 2017), Nipah, rabies, hepatitis.
Hepatitis B, like HIV, spreads via blood/sexual contact; a vaccine EXISTS for Hepatitis B but not C (UPSC 2019).
AMR drivers (UPSC 2019): antibiotic overuse in humans and livestock, poor sanitation, incomplete courses.
Wolbachia bacteria in Aedes mosquitoes reduce dengue/Zika transmission (UPSC 2023).
Eradicated/eliminated: smallpox (global, 1980), polio (India certified polio-free 2014), guinea worm (India 2000) — UPSC 2014 asked which diseases were eradicated.

newNodesToCreate.title: Immunology & Vaccine Technologies — mRNA, Viral Vector, Monoclonal Antibodies & CAR-T
prelimsNote: Vaccine types: live attenuated, inactivated (Covaxin), subunit/protein, viral vector (Covishield, Sputnik V), mRNA (Pfizer, Moderna), DNA (ZyCoV-D — world's first DNA vaccine for COVID).
Recombinant vector vaccines can be developed quickly and induce strong immunity (UPSC 2021).
Monoclonal antibodies are lab-made identical antibodies targeting one antigen.
CAR-T therapy re-engineers a patient's T cells to attack cancer; India's first, NexCAR19, approved 2023.
Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine protects against pneumonia, meningitis and sepsis; India has an indigenous PCV (UPSC 2020).

newNodesToCreate.title: Astronomy, Orbits & Space Observatories — Lagrange Points, Telescopes & Cosmology
prelimsNote: Lagrange points L1–L5: positions where gravitational forces balance; Aditya-L1 at Sun–Earth L1, James Webb at L2.
Cepheids are pulsating stars; nebulae are dust–gas clouds; pulsars are rotating neutron stars (UPSC 2023 swapped these).
Gravitational waves (LIGO, 2015) and eLISA/LISA space-based detector (UPSC 2017, 2019, 2020).
Black holes, expanding universe and cosmic microwave background are key cosmology terms (UPSC 2017).
AstroSat (2015): India's first multi-wavelength space observatory (UPSC 2016); Hubble in LEO, James Webb (infrared) at L2.
